Apple is rolling out a new beta firmware for AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, and other designated models — here are the details.

Apple rolls out new beta firmware for designated AirPods models

If your AirPods are equipped with the H2 chip, a brand-new beta firmware is now available for early access.

The build number for Apple's latest AirPods beta firmware is 9B5042a.

For reference, the current public firmware for AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Max 2, and other models is 9A348, while the newly released AirPods 5 runs on 9A350.

The new firmware is now available for AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods 5, AirPods 4, and AirPods Max 2.

It is currently unknown what changes this firmware brings. Apple may be paving the way for new features in iOS 27.1 or 27.2, or this update may primarily focus on bug fixes and performance improvements.

If you want to get an early look at the new AirPods firmware, you can opt into the beta update program from the AirPods settings page on your iPhone.

Users cannot manually trigger a firmware update, but Apple has provided guidance to help ensure automatic updates complete as quickly as possible.

  • Make sure your iPhone, iPad, or Mac is updated to the latest version of iOS, iPadOS, or macOS, with Bluetooth enabled.
  • Make sure your AirPods are connected via Bluetooth to your iPhone, iPad, or Mac.
  • Connect your iPhone, iPad, or Mac to Wi-Fi.
  • Plug your charging case into a power source.
  • Place your AirPods back in the charging case and close the lid. Keep the case lid closed, and keep your AirPods within Bluetooth range of your iPhone, iPad, or Mac.
  • Wait at least 30 minutes to allow the firmware update to complete.
  • Open the charging case lid and let your AirPods reconnect to your iPhone, iPad, or Mac.
  • Check the firmware version again.

Have you installed the new AirPods beta firmware? Let us know in the comments about any new features you've discovered.
